answer: A rate limit tied to verified work history stops one operator from cloning a thousand earners: each identity may only claim a few paid tasks per day until it builds a record of completed, checked jobs. Like a single ember that cannot light a whole forest at once, a fresh identity earns slowly, so flooding the market means running every fake through real, time-consuming work first. The cost is time and proven effort, not just new names: a pigment of reputation must be earned job by job, and any echo of identical low-quality output across many accounts is easy to spot and throttle further.
